nativeAxes.origin: Native+X east,+Z south; heading0 preserves the GMG survey south180/WNW292.5/NE45-degree bays, ENE67.5/WSW247.5-degree ladders and SSE157.5/NNW337.5-degree caisson long axis.

sourceFacts.survey: GMG GA218014, 14 June 2019, section 1.02 pp I-5–7; field visits October 2018 and May 2019
sourceFacts.verticalDatum: GMG III-9 uses low water = NN -2.05 m; tower tip NN +28.90 m
sourceFacts.basis: 2018–2019 surveyed offshore exterior. Above-water caisson is reconstructed from two7.3m-radius arcs with3.6m circle-center separation, approximately11x14m; bay offset is reconstructed from published1.9m diameter/270-degree exposed arcs and5.1m central service-room diameter. These rounded facts are not a fabrication survey. Exact corrosion/fasteners, submerged caisson, hidden interior and operating optics excluded. Static viewer water zero approximates historical NN; local floor datum−2.05m is explicit and no tide/datum conversion is claimed. The owner2026 chronology proposes relocation but does not document a completed move.

appearance.identity: Offshore riveted taper with black plinth, white/red/white shaft, red service room and three unequal-height round bays; white lantern, black domes, scalloped gallery, portholes, rivets, ladders, davit and mooring dolphins.
appearance.master: Exact historical master retained; reviewed exterior cuts real circular portholes, reconstructs almond caisson and270-degree bay intersections.
appearance.browser: Whole three-bay tower, two domes, service-room openings, scalloped gallery, lantern, finial, two ladders, mooring posts and davit retained. Rivet density and curved subdivisions reduce with distance.
